Subject: Request: temporary waiver of stabilization surcharge + redline attached

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We ran the expected consumption numbers through our finance team and we have one ask on the pricing schedule before we can finalize. AcmeAI is concerned about the "stabilization surcharge" language in Exhibit B — specifically the automatic step-up that triggers if monthly usage exceeds the forecast by >25%. For our Q4 pilot we requested a temporary waiver or a softer ramp so our unit economics aren't materially impacted while we instrument logging and prefetch caches.

Attached is a short redline (redlines_acme_v3.pdf) that shows our suggested edits: a 90-day waiver from effective date OR a 15% buffer before the surcharge applies, plus a mutual review at day 60.

Can your legal team confirm whether Redwood can agree to a temporary waiver or the buffer approach? If needed, we can accept a time-limited surcharge with a cap (no more than +10% on month-over-month bill) in exchange for a 12-month minimum commitment. We're trying to avoid an up-front price shock for the pilot.

Appreciate a quick read — we're on an internal procurement deadline and would like to get the order form approved by 12/3.

Thanks,
Maya Rana
Procurement Manager
AcmeAI

Attachment: redlines_acme_v3.pdf (pdf, 42 KB)
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary waiver of stabilization surcharge + redline attached

Hi Maya / Tom / Lina —

Appreciate the clear redline. We're sympathetic to avoiding a sudden surcharge during a pilot. Two quick notes from the commercial side: 

1) Waiver window: we can offer a 60-day full waiver from the effective date (not 90) combined with a single one-time cap on exposure equal to one month of estimated usage. That keeps our risk limited while giving you runway to instrument.

2) Buffer: alternatively, if you prefer a buffer instead of a pure waiver, Redwood can accept a 20% buffer before the surcharge triggers (we'd propose the surcharge steps at +20% and +40% with a hard cap at +10% bill impact per month once triggered).

3) Commitment trade: in both cases we'd ask for a modest minimum spend true-up for the first 12 months to balance collection risk — we can model this conservatively in the attached tracker (pricing_schedule_tracker.xlsx).

I've looped in Marissa (legal ops) and Rishi (pricing) to weigh in on contract language and unit economics. If AcmeAI is comfortable with either option, we can prepare a succinct amendment to Exhibit B and route for signatures (DocuSign link provided when ready).

Quick ask: Tom, if you can confirm whether AcmeAI prefers the 60-day waiver + capped exposure or the buffer with capped monthly impact, we will convert to redline language today.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Commercial Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary waiver of stabilization surcharge + redline attached

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick reply and the alternative paths. A couple of legal redline points from our side after reviewing your proposed options: 

- We prefer the buffer approach (15% or 20%) to a full waiver since it better aligns incentives, but we need the following contract clarifications in Exhibit B:
  * Remove the unilateral price-adjustment clause that allows Redwood to alter surcharge thresholds without mutual written consent.
  * Define the calculation methodology for "monthly usage" (UTC timestamps vs billing period, how retries/duplicates are counted) to avoid disputes.
  * Add a mutual review clause at 60 days with a 10-business-day good-faith negotiation window; if tied, revert to the originally forecasted rates for the next billing period rather than an automatic increase.

- On minimums: AcmeAI cannot commit to a 12-month hard minimum for the pilot stage. We can agree to a 6-month soft commitment with a capped true-up (up to 20% of projected spend) if the buffer approach is adopted.

I've inserted inline comments in your PDF redline and attached our clean language suggestions. If Redwood can accept these guardrails, we can execute quickly.

Regards,
Tom Reynolds
Senior Counsel, AcmeAI

Attachment: acme_inline_comments.pdf (pdf, 9 KB)

Tom / Maya / Lina —

Thanks for the comments and for preferring the buffer approach — that helps. From a contract language perspective Redwood can accept the following, subject to commercial confirmation from Rishi: 

1) Surcharge threshold: replace the unilateral language with "Surcharge Thresholds shall only be amended by written agreement signed by both Parties."

2) Usage definition: add a short clause: "Monthly Usage means the total number of billed inference units processed by Redwood during a billing period, excluding retries where the same request ID is processed more than once; timestamps are assessed in UTC for billing alignment."

3) Mutual review: 60-day review followed by a 10-business-day negotiation window; if Parties cannot agree, then for the following billing period charges shall be calculated using the previously forecasted rates (no automatic escalations).

4) Minimums: convert the 12-month hard minimum request to a 6-month soft commitment with a capped true-up equal to 20% of projected spend. We will reflect the exact numbers in Exhibit B table.

Next steps: Rishi will confirm the exact buffer numbers (we proposed 20% buffer & +10% max monthly bill step). If AcmeAI accepts, we will prepare an amendment to Exhibit B (clean + redline) and route via DocuSign.

Vanessa, will you please confirm the commercial trade-off live and I will prepare the legal redline this afternoon?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
